gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker 737 (24K, 140 W), which ChatGPT called 'best overall' and 'best premium', is sold out at Anker US today, or that the cheapest 20,000 mAh banks rated 45 W or more cost $36.99 (INIU Carry 45W) and $39.99 (Baseus EnerFill FC11) at the makers' own stores on 2026-11-13, against $46.99 to $229.99 for ChatGPT's picks, when Valve's own charger is 45 W.
standout_why: Compared against itechguides (cited in one chat; lists Anker 87W $69.99, INIU 65W $42.29, UGREEN 25K 145W $79.99, Anker 25K 165W $119.99, JUOVI $39.99; no Anker 737, no price per Wh, no 45 W-floor product), gamingonbatteries best-power-bank-steam-deck (cited; no prices for any product, only ranges like '$40-$70 for 45W-class'; lists the Anker 737 as a 'Check on Amazon' link with no stock note), vgkami (cited; no prices at all) and rallynomics (cited; has Anker Prime 26K $229.99, Anker 25K 165W $119.99/$104.99, UGREEN 130W $59.99, INIU 25,000 mAh 100W $66.99; no Anker 737 stock status, no price per Wh, no 45 W budget banks). None says the 737 is sold out or names a sub-$40 bank that meets Valve's 45 W spec. Our own page still lists the 737 at $109.99.
decides: It drops the Anker 737 from the picks: it is sold out at Anker US, yet ChatGPT made it 'best overall' in one chat and 'best premium' in another, and our page lists it. Valve specifies a 45 W PD 3.0 supply, so wattage above 45 W adds nothing for the Deck alone. That makes this a capacity-per-dollar decision. The budget floor is $36.99 to $39.99 for 20,000 mAh (INIU Carry 45W, Baseus FC11, both with built-in cables). Our Baseus EnerFill FC41 25,000 mAh at $79.99 undercuts the UGREEN 25,000 mAh 165W ($109.99 today, not the $74.99 ChatGPT showed) by $30 at the same capacity with built-in cables. INIU's Cougar 65W at $46.99 is still a sound value pick, but it is not the cheapest bank that charges the Deck at its full 45 W.
